answer: A registry can issue each agent a single cipher-signed identity only after a hardware attestation proves a distinct device, then require that identity to earn trust slowly: new identities start in a shallow lagoon of limited privileges and gain access only after a history of useful, verified work. A grove of established agents cross-checks each other's claims, so one operator spinning up thousands of clones must buy thousands of devices and wait out the same slow ramp for each, turning a cheap flood into a costly, visible crawl.
